'''Ajoy Kumar Ghatak''' is an Indian [[physicist]] and author of physics textbooks.

Ghatak has written over 170 research papers and more than 20 books. His undergraduate textbook on ''Optics''<ref name=":0">{{cite book | last=Ghatak | first=Ajoy | title=Optics | publisher=McGraw-Hill Education | publication-place=New York, NY | date=2009-03-23 | isbn=978-0-07-338048-3 | page=}}</ref> has been translated to Chinese and Persian and his monograph on ''Inhomogeneous Optical Waveguides''<ref>{{cite book | last1=Sodha | first1=M. S. | last2=Ghatak | first2=Ajoy | title=Inhomogeneous Optical Waveguides | publisher=Springer | publication-place=New York NY | date=1977 | isbn=978-0-306-30916-8 | page=}}</ref> (coauthored with Professor Sodha) has been translated to Chinese and Russian.<ref>{{Citation | url=http://www.mirandahouse.ac.in/DSKC/ALOP_ASIA_2006_REPORT.pdf | title=Miranda House events | access-date=8 November 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721150331/http://www.mirandahouse.ac.in/DSKC/ALOP_ASIA_2006_REPORT.pdf | archive-date=21 July 2011 | url-status=dead | df=dmy-all }}</ref> 

In 1995, he was elected Fellow of the [[Optica (society)]] "for distinguished service to optics education and for his contribution to the understanding of propagation characteristics of gradient index media, fibers and integrated optical devices".<ref name="ico" />

== Education ==
He received his M.Sc. from [[Delhi University]] and Ph.D. from [[Cornell University]].<ref name=phd>
{{cite thesis |type=Ph.D. thesis |publisher=Cornell University |publication-place= |last=Ghatak |first=Ajoy |date=1964 |title=Non linear prompt neutron kinetics in multigroup diffusion theory |oclc=77223065 |hdl= |doi= |osti= |url= }}
</ref>

== Career ==
Ghatak joined the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi]] in 1966.<ref name="ico">{{Citation | url=http://www.ico-optics.org/ico_jan99.html | title=Ajoy Ghatak biography | publisher=[[International Commission for Optics]] | access-date=7 November 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100713025201/http://www.ico-optics.org/ico_jan99.html | archive-date=13 July 2010 | url-status=dead }}</ref> He retired as an Emeritus Professor of Physics at IIT Delhi in 2007.<ref>{{Citation|title=IIT Kharagpur's biography on Ajoy Ghatak |url=http://www.phy.iitkgp.ernet.in/ptaccd2/Speakers_Biodata/AKGhatak_Bio.pdf |publisher=[[Indian Institute of Technology]] |access-date=8 November 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110302102415/http://www.phy.iitkgp.ernet.in/ptaccd2/Speakers_Biodata/AKGhatak_Bio.pdf |archive-date=2 March 2011 }}</ref>

Ghatak served as the President of the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] for the duration 2021 - 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Past Presidents [1981 - Till Date], NASI Website |url=https://nasi.ac.in/president## |url-status=live |access-date=February 28, 2026 |website=[[National Academy of Sciences, India]]}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|title=NASI Council 2021-22|url=http://nasi.nic.in/council.htm }}</ref> He also spends his time writing books and doing special guest lectures at universities and colleges in India and internationally.<ref>{{Citation|title=BESU Events 2010 |url=http://www.becs.ac.in/events-2010.html |access-date=8 November 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101118003159/http://www.becs.ac.in/events-2010.html |archive-date=18 November 2010 }}</ref><ref>{{Citation|title=SPIE Events |url=http://spiedcechapter.dce.edu/archive/news18.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100720005617/http://spiedcechapter.dce.edu/archive/news18.php |url-status=dead |archive-date=20 July 2010 |access-date=8 November 2010 }}</ref> In recent years, he has taken a keen interest in bringing the genius of [[Albert Einstein]] to the wider public and was invited to present a [[TEDx]] talk, "Inside Einstein's mind"<ref>Archived at [https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211205/p9n_Mr80elg Ghostarchive]{{cbignore}} and the [https://web.archive.org/web/20171129062845/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p9n_Mr80elg&gl=US&hl=en Wayback Machine]{{cbignore}}: {{cite web| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p9n_Mr80elg| title = Inside Einstein's mind, E=mc^2 {{!}} Ajoy Ghatak {{!}} TEDxJIIT | website=[[YouTube]]| date=14 November 2017 }}{{cbignore}}</ref> in 2017.

== Selected awards and honors ==
* [[Optica (society)]] Sang Soo Lee Award (2020) "For his seminal role in the development of fiber optics and guided wave photonics and for pioneering optics education in India."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sang Soo Lee Award|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/sangsooleeaward/|url-status=live|website=The Optical Society|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141202130108/http://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/sangsooleeaward/|archive-date=2 December 2014|access-date=5 April 2021}}</ref>
*[[SPIE]] Educator Award (2008) "in recognition of outstanding contributions to optics education"<ref>{{Citation | title=SPIE Educator Award | url=http://spie.org/x3069.xml | access-date=8 November 2010 }}</ref>
*[[DSc|DSc (Honoris causa)]] (2007) from [[University of Burdwan]]<ref name=":0" />
* Esther Hoffman Beller Medal (2003) of the [[Optica (society)]] "for outstanding contributions to optical science and engineering education"<ref>{{Citation | title=OSA's Esther Hoffman Beller Medal | url=http://www.osa.org/Awards_and_Grants/Awards/Award_Description/estherbeller/default.aspx | access-date=8 November 2010 }}</ref>
* Galileo Galilei Award (1998) of the [[International Commission for Optics]] "for outstanding contributions to the field of optics which are achieved under comparatively unfavorable circumstances"<ref>{{Citation|title=ICO Galileo Galilei Award |url=http://www.ico-optics.org/awards.html#galileo |access-date=8 November 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110709212802/http://www.ico-optics.org/awards.html |archive-date=9 July 2011 }}</ref>
* [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology|S. S. Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]] – Physical Sciences (1979) of the [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] "for significant work in the field of inhomogeneous optical wave-guides, theory of aberrations for optical systems comprising inhomogeneous media and self-focussing of laser beams"<ref>{{Citation | title=S. S. Bhatnagar award for Physical Sciences | url=http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/Physical_SCIENCES.htm | access-date=8 November 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927141401/http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/Physical_SCIENCES.htm | archive-date=27 September 2011 | url-status=dead | df=dmy-all }}</ref>
